suitability: Common terms and recap available on every route; two or more defensible responses; concrete details include unnamed receiver, unconfirmed testimony, reciprocal promise and separated family. Students can formulate and test principles without outside research.
history: Treaty fixed. Case, characters, procedures, local authority and all branch outcomes invented. No claimed ancient quotation. No modern universal refugee-rights framework attributed to the treaty.
passes: Opening puts the threatened return within the first scene. Each option has a distinct response and major choices return later. Scenes change information, stakes, policy or accountability; listener close-ups hold fear and respect before replies. Humor humanizes without mocking vulnerability.
assets: Reuse hybrid Hepting/Lin and classroom/Egyptian courtyard. Three original polished SVG characters through shared builder. No music, audio or new bitmap images. Cord and papers narrated/mimed.
assessment: Four knowledge MCQs separate from six moral choices. Decision Note and fortnightly presentation handoff in teaching-guide.html. No Canvas posting.
